curriculum.lesson_evidence: Sharing movement work means performing for an audience and responding respectfully. Performers prepare, begin with a still shape, move with focus and finish with a held pose. Audience members watch quietly, clap kindly and give feedback as two stars and a wish. Performers may choose not to be watched closely: they can perform for one person or share their plan instead.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write one star and one wish for a dancer who moved smoothly but looked at the floor the whole time.

FEEDBACK
Star: smooth, controlled movements. Wish: lift your head and look at the audience. Feedback names a specific strength and one idea to improve.

WATCH FOR
Believing audience feedback means judging the dancer. Feedback helps performers improve and should always be kind and specific.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Rehearse and share your sequence or dance with an audience. Record two stars and a wish, make one change and perform again. Write a short reflection on how you felt before and after, and what helped.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.
